----Respondent For Petitioner(s) : Mr. Dhirendra Singh, Sr. Adv.
 assisted by Mr. Abhishek Sharma and  Ms. Priyanka Borana For Respondent(s) : Mr. Salim Khan, P.P.
For Complainant (s) : Mr. SK Dadhich  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 18/09/2023

This application for bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner who has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.52/2023, registered at Police Station Pipar City, District Jodhpur Rural, for offences under Sections 498A, 304B & 406 IPC.
As per prosecution, complainant- Anda Ram submitted a written report dated 11.02.2023 stating inter alia that his daughter deceased- Kanchan was married to the present petitioner on 02.12.2016.
Deceased- Kanchan was subjected to mental and physical cruelty at the hands of the present petitioner, in connection with dowry demand since the date of the marriage.
As per prosecution, the petitioner was demanding a car of Rs.5,00,000/- as dowry and threatened that if the demand is not fulfilled, he will not keep the deceased with him.

Thereupon, a [2023:RJ-JD:30079] (2 of 5)
[CRLMB-10933/2023] sum of Rs.1,00,00/- was given to the petitioner by the family of the deceased.
As per prosecution, on 10.02.2023, son of the complainant namely Mana Ram received a call from the deceased informing that she has been beaten by the elder brother of the petitioner.

On 11.02.2023, the niece of the complainant received a call from the elder brother of the petitioner,

sentences.text: The complainant demanded legal action against the petitioner by way of submitting a written complaint before PS Pipar City for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 304B and 406 IPC.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the FIR is based on false and fabricated facts.
Learned counsel further submitted that the investigating agency after making thorough investigation in the matter has already submitted challan before competent criminal court on 08.05.2023.

Drawing attention of the Court towards the challan papers, learned counsel submitted that the CCTV cameras installed in the house of the petitioner have been analysed by the investigating agency and the analysis whereof, made by the investigating agency does not reflect any untoward behaviour of the petitioner towards the deceased.

Learned counsel also submitted that the CCTV footage as analysed in the challan papers shows that the deceased committed suicide by consuming insecticide/ poision without any provocation/ instigation from the petitioner or any of his family members.

Learned counsel contended that the statements of the deceased were recorded by one Sarwar Khan,
Head Constable, [2023:RJ-JD:30079] (3 of 5) [CRLMB-10933/2023] who received an information in this regard on his Whatsapp at 3:54 pm, in MDM Hospital Jodhpur soon before her death,
wherein she stated that she consumed insecticide/ poison in ignorance and did not allege anything against anyone.
Learned counsel further submitted that a thorough scanning of the challan papers would reveal that the behaviour of the petitioner and his family members on the date of alleged incident towards deceased was normal and she was not ill treated by them.

Learned counsel submitted that admittedly, the marriage of the petitioner was solemnised with the deceased in the year 2016 and it is unusual that she would be subjected to cruelty or harassment in connection with dowry demand after so many years of the marriage.
Learned counsel vehemently submitted that there is no material available on record indicating that the deceased was subjected to cruelty or ill treatment in connection with demand for dowry.

To fortify this contention, the Court was requested to take into consideration the statement of Moinnudin (an independent witness) recorded under Section 161 CrPC and statement of Mr. Sarwar Khan (Head Constable) coupled with the analysis of CCTV footage made by investigating agency in the challan.
On these grounds, learned counsel implored the Court to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant vehemently opposed the bail application and fervently submitted that the complainant in the written complaint has stated that the deceased was subjected to cruelty and harassment by the present petitioner, since the demand of dowry [2023:RJ-JD:30079] (4 of 5) [CRLMB-10933/2023] was not fulfilled.
Attention was drawn towards specific averment in the complaint that the demand of dowry could not be fulfilled as it was beyond the complainant's capacity.

Learned counsel drew attention of the Court towards the dead body inspection report (fard surathal laash) prepared by the police and post mortem report of the deceased prepared by Medical Board,
MDM Hospital, Jodhpur showing number of injuries on the body of the deceased.

Further attention was drawn towards the statements of Aarti, wife of Mana Ram, recorded under Section 161 CrPC wherein she stated that on 10.02.2023, on receiving call from her mother in law informing that health condition of deceased is not well, she visited her before she was taken to hospital by her in laws, whereupon the deceased told Aarti that 'mere se roz roz maar nahi khaayi jaati..'.

Attention of the Court was further drawn towards the statements of complainant, Mana Ram (brother of deceased) and Smt. Santosh (mother of deceased), recorded under Section 161 CrPC to urge that the deceased committed suicide being perturbed by the cruel behaviour of the petitioner.

On these grounds, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant prayed that looking to the seriousness of the accusations levelled against the petitioner, he does not deserve indulgence of bail in the present case.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the complainant.
Perused the material available on record.

[2023:RJ-JD:30079] (5 of 5) [CRLMB-10933/2023] Having considered facts and circumstances of the case and challan papers, this Court prima facie finds that the death of the deceased has taken place in unnatural circumstances within 7 years of marriage; serious allegations of demand of dowry soon before her death and beating the deceased have been levelled against the petitioner; ante mortem injuries were found in dead body inspection report (fard surathal laash) and post mortem report; statements of deceased recorded by Sarwar Khan recorded in MDM Hospital and CCTV footage of a particular day cannot be considered conclusive to decide the allegation of continuous harassment and cruelty against the petitioner in connection with dowry demand, even otherwise,
relevance of the statements of the deceased and CCTV footage and the analysis whereof, is a subject matter to be decided and considered by the trial court during the course of trial, based on the evidence produced before it; at this stage, this Court prima facie finds that the prosecution has succeeded successfully in establishing a case against the petitioner and therefore, the bail application does not deserve to be allowed.
Accordingly, the present Criminal Misc. Bail Application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. is dismissed.
It is however, made clear that findings recorded / observations made above are for limited purposes of adjudication of bail application.
The trial court shall not get prejudice by the same.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J /Prashant/-
